bio: I’m a Computer Science graduate from Penn State with a strong foundation in backend systems, embedded software, and full-stack development. My work spans low-level systems programming, AI/LLM integration, and modern web technologies. At Amphenol, I developed C++ firmware utilities and a custom PID control algorithm for high-speed cable testing, working hands-on with I²C devices like the PCA9685 and MPC9600. In open source, I volunteer with Greenstand for their TreeTracker Wallet App, where I led the BDD test infrastructure (WebdriverIO + Cucumber in TypeScript), wrote step definitions against the real UI and APIs, and shipped parallel E2E runs with embedded videos/screenshots for fast triage. I also contribute to OpenHands, where I fixed a prompt-input autosize bug by refactoring height measurement and debouncing to deliver consistent multi-line typing across browsers. As a full-stack developer, I’ve built data-driven web platforms using the MERN stack and MySQL, including a B2B eCommerce system and dynamic support ticketing workflows. My AI projects include integrating the OpenAI API into real-world applications with semantic search and typewriter-style response rendering. On campus, I led tutoring sessions in systems programming, data structures, and object-oriented design at the Academic Excellence Center. I’ve also engineered a peer-to-peer file sharing network, an AR iOS furniture layout app with RealityKit, and a custom memory allocator in C. I’m passionate about building scalable, user-centric systems—from embedded tools to end-to-end platforms—and excited to contribute to engineering teams solving real-world problems.
skills: Java, React.js, Next.js, Node.js, Express.js, JavaScript, Python, C++, C, SQL, OpenAI API, Cursor, Prompt Engineering, MongoDB, Verilog, I2C, Git, HTML, CSS, ARKit, RealityKit, Swift, SwiftUI

projects.name: AI Portfolio Website
projects.description: An AI-powered personal portfolio website featuring an interactive ChatGPT stlye chatbot that answers recruiter questions using a custom RAG pipeline and OpenAI's GPT-4o.
projects.details: I engineered a full-stack AI portfolio website that integrates a ChatGPT-style assistant capable of answering dynamic questions about my background, experience, and projects. Built with a custom Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system, the chatbot uses OpenAI’s `text-embedding-ada-002` model for semantic search over embedded content chunks and GPT-4o for natural language generation. I implemented cosine similarity logic, fine-tuned scoring heuristics, and a dual-layer chunking system for context resolution. On the frontend, I recreated the ChatGPT UI using React and CSS Modules, with features like dynamic message typing, mobile responsiveness, animated modals, and form-to-email integration via Formspree. I handled rate limiting, edge case fallbacks, and OpenAI error scenarios with user-friendly responses. The site includes full SEO metadata, Open Graph image support, and deployment to Vercel using environment variables and statically served assets for optimal performance.

projects.name: NittanyBusiness E-Commerce Website
projects.description: A full-stack B2B e-commerce platform built to streamline procurement for SMEs by connecting them with suppliers through an intuitive interface and optimized backend infrastructure.
projects.details: I designed an end-to-end B2B e-commerce procurement platform tailored for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) facing inefficient procurement processes and limited supplier access. I developed both the frontend and backend using React.js, Node.js, and Express.js, implementing core features such as user authentication, product listings, and order management. To ensure responsive and scalable performance, I built and optimized a REST API that enabled real-time data retrieval, significantly reducing response times and improving access to product and transaction information. I also designed a normalized logical database schema to enhance query efficiency and eliminate redundant data storage. Additionally, I created an interactive user interface for business owners and suppliers, which improved user engagement and minimized onboarding friction for new users.

projects.name: Peer-to-Peer File Sharing System
projects.description: A Python-based P2P file-sharing network with chunked transfers, multi-threaded downloads, and built-in integrity checks for fast and reliable file distribution.
projects.details: I designed a peer-to-peer (P2P) file-sharing network in Python, featuring a central server and multiple peers to enable efficient and decentralized file distribution. The system uses a chunk-based approach to split large files, allowing simultaneous downloads from multiple peers, which significantly improves overall download speed. I implemented multi-threading to handle parallel connections smoothly and ensure scalability. To maintain data integrity, I integrated hashing-based checks that verify the accuracy of downloaded chunks and discard any corrupted data.

projects.name: Causal Consistency Simulation
projects.description: A Python-based distributed system that simulates causal consistency across multiple data centers using Lamport clocks and dependency tracking.
projects.details: I developed a distributed system simulation to demonstrate causal consistency using three interlinked data centers. Each datacenter tracks dependencies between write operations using Lamport clocks to maintain causality and ensure that messages are delivered in a consistent order. I implemented FIFO message delivery and Lamport timestamping to enforce correct inter-datacenter communication. The system models realistic delay patterns and highlights how causally-related writes are respected across the network even when operating asynchronously. This helped me deepen my understanding of consistency models and their tradeoffs in distributed architectures.

projects.name: Dynamic Storage Allocator
projects.description: A custom C dynamic memory allocator featuring optimized malloc/realloc/free, segregated free lists, and a heap consistency checker for robust memory management.
projects.details: I developed a dynamic memory allocator for C programs by implementing custom versions of malloc, realloc, and free, with a focus on optimizing space utilization and throughput. This was achieved through techniques such as block header/footer optimization, coalescing of free blocks, and the use of size-based segregated linked lists for efficient allocation. To ensure reliable memory management, I also created a heap consistency checker that runs in debugging mode to detect and resolve heap inconsistencies.

projects.name: Expense Tracker App
projects.description: A MERN stack expense tracker web app with real-time transaction updates and seamless backend integration for efficient personal finance management.
projects.details: I developed a user-friendly expense tracker web application using the MERN stack, enabling users to effortlessly manage and track their finances. The frontend was built with React.js, providing a responsive interface with real-time updates to transactions and balances in the DOM. On the backend, I implemented business logic using Node.js and Express.js to handle data storage and integrated the application with MongoDB for efficient and reliable data management.

projects.name: Linear Device Library
projects.description: A C-based Linux utility that combines 16 JBODs into a 1 MB linear device with read/write support, LRU caching, and TCP networking for efficient storage access.
projects.details: I designed and developed a Linux mdadm-style utility in C to configure 16 JBOD devices, each 64 KB in size, into a single coherent 1 MB linear storage device. I implemented core read and write functionalities that allowed access to the storage architecture using a user-provided buffer. To enhance performance and flexibility, I introduced an LRU caching mechanism that reduced the cost of JBOD operations by 30%, and added networking support by developing a client component to communicate with the embedded JBOD server over TCP.

projects.name: Mini CPU
projects.description: A Verilog-based 5-stage MIPS pipeline with ALU-to-ALU data forwarding and hazard resolution for optimized execution of R-type instructions.
projects.details: I designed and developed a comprehensive 5-stage MIPS pipeline in Verilog to execute R-type arithmetic instructions efficiently. To optimize CPU performance and ensure accurate data processing, I implemented data-forwarding modules using a state machine, enabling ALU-to-ALU forwarding and effective handling of data hazards. This included integrating detailed case handling to support accurate and reliable data manipulation across pipeline stages.

projects.name: Course Scheduler App
projects.description: A database-driven course scheduler with role-based access, built using OOP principles, SQL, and a tabbed GUI for organized course and student management.
projects.details: I created a database-driven course scheduler application that supports both administrative and student authorizations, applying object-oriented programming principles throughout the design. I used SQL to query student, course, and schedule data from an Apache Derby database, ensuring accurate and efficient data retrieval. To enhance user experience, I designed a tabbed layout graphical user interface (GUI) that presents information in a clear and organized manner.

projects.name: Furniture Store App
projects.description: An iOS AR app for virtual room decor that lets users place, scale, and move life-size furniture models in real-world spaces with saved layouts and guided setup.
projects.details: I created an immersive iOS virtual room decor app designed to help users plan furniture placement in their actual living spaces, eliminating the need to visit multiple furniture stores. The app features a picture menu at the bottom of the interface, allowing users to select and place life-sized furniture models in the real world with a tap. I enhanced these models with functionality for scaling, rotation, and movement to provide a realistic and flexible design experience. To support new users, I integrated an AR Coaching Overlay that guides them through app setup and room scanning. The app also includes persistence to save virtual room maps, displays real-time mapping status for debugging, and offers a clear button to delete saved maps along with an undo button to remove the last added model.

projects.name: Measurement App
projects.description: An iOS AR measurement app that lets users mark two points in the real world to calculate distances, with logging, undo, and guided setup features.
projects.details: I created an iOS virtual measurement app that allows users to measure the distance between two real-world points using augmented reality, supported by an AR Coaching Overlay for guided setup. Users can place two model entities with a tap to mark the points, and the app calculates and displays the distance in meters. I implemented a logging feature to store all measurement records, along with a clear button to reset the log and an undo button to remove the last entry, enhancing the overall user experience.

experience.work: I led the BDD testing infrastructure for the TreeTracker Wallet App by planning milestones with the VP of Engineering, creating and managing GitHub issues, and driving incremental delivery. I integrated WebdriverIO and Cucumber in TypeScript to run parallel end-to-end tests with automatic video and screenshot capture and readable HTML reports. I wrote step definitions that exercise the real UI, call backend APIs, and assert user-visible outcomes to validate full feature flows end to end. I also consolidated test artifacts by embedding per-scenario videos and failing-step screenshots directly into the Cucumber HTML report, speeding triage and creating a single source of truth for test results.

I developed a C++ command-line interface to communicate with I2C devices, PWM controllers, and TC amplifier chips, leveraging their capabilities for high-speed cable thermal testing. I engineered robust wrapper functions that provided seamless access to all chip features according to their datasheet specifications, ensuring reliable control and future scalability. To validate the setup, I created a testing environment using PWM logic to simulate real-world conditions and facilitate empirical data analysis prior to integration with the thermostream system. Additionally, I programmed a customized PID control algorithm that improved temperature correction accuracy from ±7°C to ±0.5°C, meeting stringent customer requirements.

Open-Source Contributions.description: OpenHands is an open-source platform for AI software-development agents. I am a contributor and focused on frontend reliability and UX quality.
Open-Source Contributions.details: Resolved a prompt-box resize bug that caused overflow on long messages by refactoring height measurement logic, adding tolerance handling, and debouncing resize events in React/TypeScript to ensure consistent multi-line behavior across browsers. The fix stabilized typing and paste experiences and eliminated layout jumps in the prompt area.
